Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly render its surfaces with a chalk-like appearance, rather than merely adding grain or a filter to the source image?
node.criteria: Pass if, compared with the source, visible surface marks or tonal treatment make the image read as rendered with chalk. Fail if the source’s surface appearance remains or the only change is generic grain or filtering that does not produce a chalk-like rendering. Unknown only if the surface treatment cannot be observed.
node.endpoint: The drawing has visibly chalk-like surface marks or tonal treatment.
node.necessity: The instruction specifies that the drawing is made from chalk; a drawing without a visibly chalk-like rendering does not fulfill that requested material appearance.

node_traces.evidence: Compared with the source photograph, the edited image has a visibly drawn, chalk-like treatment: broad smudged tonal strokes across the sky, ground, and foliage, with soft sketchy outlines and textured marks on the giraffes. The surfaces no longer read as the source's photographic rendering.
